subject: medkit
leg: control: Valve's own against the brief
label: medkit.mdl, in the place of the game's models/w_medkit.mdl

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_crowbar.mdl, models/w_shotgun.mdl, models/snapbug.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 3 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked C, D, C where the asset was C, A, D: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: The outline matches the brief's words: a low, flat white case about 35 by 26 units, with bevelled top edges and a carry strap looping off one side. In the front, back, left and right views the case sits flat on the floor, and the strap does not stick out beyond the brief's shape. The top view shows the case as a squarish block, with the strap trailing from one edge.

M2.reason: Measured size is 34.6 x 26.4 x 6.8 against the brief's 35 x 26 x 7, a 3.3% offset, well within 15%.

M3.reason: Parts the brief asks for, checked down to the small ones: the white case (one body); the red cross (one, painted on the top, reads clearly in the top and front-right views); the FIRST AID lettering (one line, painted on the top, legible in the top and front-right views); the carry strap (one loop, present in the top, front-left and back-right views). The brief names no claws, teeth, rivets, tabs or round parts. The dark recessed panel with grey clip and red and green lights is extra, not asked for, and adds nothing wrong.

M4.reason: White case with a red cross and red lettering, a dark grey recessed panel, and a brown-grey woven strap. Each region reads as its material: painted plastic or metal, cloth. The strap's checker pattern reads as woven cloth; the brief gives no colour for it, so nothing is contradicted.

M5.reason: The cross, the FIRST AID lettering and the red edge arrows are all in their places on the top and sides, and they stay sharp at this scale. The lettering is a little soft in the front-left view but it reads. The strap's mottled texture and the case's grain are plausible, not smeared.

M6.reason: Capped by the line-up test, as the rubric directs for this measure. In the line-up the asset is one of A to D beside three of Half-Life's own; judges picked the wrong one twice in three readings, so it passes as one of the game's.

M7.reason: The case lies flat on its origin, as the brief says, at a height of 6.8 units with its base on the floor. It is upright, with the red cross on the top face. The front and back are not named in the brief, and the top lettering's orientation is charged under M5, not here.

M8.reason: 99 triangles, equal to the median of Half-Life's props of its kind, well under twice it. The check reports no errors. Nothing is open or floating in the views a player sees: the strap meets the case at its edges, and the case's bottom sits on the floor. The 'Below' view is blank, so the underside is open, but a player lying or standing above the kit never sees it, and that is Valve's practice under the rubric.
